subject: KV reuse credits & streaming proration — Ledger.ai pilot
messages:
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha@ledger.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@ledger.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Question on KV cache crediting + streaming billing for pilot

Marcus — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Two quick billing questions the finance team asked me to confirm before we move to signature:

1) KV cache reuse: Our use case heavily relies on long-lived chat sessions where the model will reuse a lot of prefix context (customer history) across calls. Does Redwood apply "KV-reuse credits" or any deduction for tokens that are not re-generated because they're served from the KV cache? In other words, if we send a 12k prefix but the model only emits 40 tokens of new text, will we be billed for the full 12k input every single call?

2) Streaming proration: We stream incremental chunks back to the client. If a stream is cut off early (client disconnects after receiving partial response), do you bill per-chunk emitted or only for the tokens actually generated server-side until the cut? Procurement is worried about unpredictable burst costs during product testing.

We are looking at a 3-month pilot: ~12k contexts, ~120k gen tokens/month expected, but bursts to 2M gen tokens on testing days. Also attaching a short workbook with sample traffic if that helps. Can you point to how this would be metered and how rounding/quantum rules apply (e.g. per-10-token buckets vs per-100)?

Thanks — if it helps, Ben on your team is our main contact for pricing.

— Aisha
Lead Product Ops, Ledger.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha@ledger.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Question on KV cache crediting + streaming billing for pilot

Hi Aisha — great questions, thanks for the workbook (received). Short answers up front:

- KV cache: you are billed for model execution tokens (input+output) by default. However, for long-lived sessions where we can deterministically reuse KV state across calls without re-encoding, we offer a KV-reuse credit applied at the invoice level for pilot/committed customers. That credit is not automatic on the hosted meter but is applied as a post-hoc adjustment tied to the committed tier (details below).

- Streaming proration: we bill on actually generated tokens. If the server stops generating because the client disconnected mid-stream, you are only billed for the tokens the model produced and committed (we measure at the token generation endpoint). However, there is a minimum billing quantum that can affect micro interactions (see rounding).

Rounding/quantum: our public meter uses a 10-token quantum for generation and a 1-token quantum for input; however, for committed customers we can set the generation quantum to 5 or 20 tokens depending on the negotiated SKU to better match your pattern. For example, with a 10-token quantum a 7-token generation is rounded up to 10.

I'll loop Ben and Marissa (pricing) to propose a simple committed structure that factors in KV credits and burst smoothing. I can do a quick sample calc after they chime in.

Best,
Marcus
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: KV reuse crediting + streaming — pricing sketch for Ledger.ai (internal)

Marcus / Ben — drafting proposed terms to share with Aisha. Key assumptions from their workbook: average context 12k tokens, average generation per call 40 tokens, baseline calls/month ~3k (=> ~120k gen tokens), periodic daily stress tests with up to 2M gen tokens. They want protection from burst volatility and recognition for repeated context reuse.

Pricing sketch (pilot, three months):
- Committed tier: $X/month credit-equivalent for 150k gen tokens + 1M token burst buffer. Any usage above the committed gen tokens billed at list gen rate.
- KV-reuse credit: we calculate a KV-reuse factor per-session by sampling the session delta (how many input tokens needed to be re-encoded). For pilot customers we propose a 60% KV credit on input tokens when measured reuse > 50% across a session cohort. Implementation: we run sampling on a daily basis and post an invoice credit aligned to the monthly bill. Example: if ledger shows 12k inputs but 60% of those tokens were satisfied from cache, the invoice line will reduce billed input tokens by 60% * input_tokens_sampled. This is a non-metered invoice credit (applied after usage is recorded).
- Streaming proration: billed for actual generated tokens; minimum quantum for pilot: 10-token generation quantum.
- Burst smoothing / overage protection: for the 3-month pilot we propose a negotiated overage cap (e.g., max additional $Y per stress day) or a committed burst pool that draws down before per-token overage applies. This can be structured as an add-on credit bucket (pre-paid).

Rounding examples (explicit):
- 40 generated tokens with 10-token quantum => billed 40 (no rounding).
- 7 generated tokens => billed 10.
- Input 12k tokens, 60% KV reuse credit => billed input tokens = 4.8k (invoice adjustment) + generator tokens as above.

Actionables: Marcus to confirm if Ledger will accept post-hoc KV credits (vs. live meter changes). Ben to produce a draft SOW and updated workbook with line-item math. I attached a quick workbook and SOW draft.

— Marissa
Senior Pricing Manager — Redwood Inference

On attachments:
- redwood_kv-credit-workbook.xlsx (sample calculations & scenarios)
- SOW-draft.pdf (pilot terms draft)
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha@ledger.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@ledger.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: KV reuse credits & streaming proration — Ledger.ai pilot

Thanks — this is helpful and the worked examples make sense. A few clarifications before procurement signs off:

1) Post-hoc credit mechanism: procurement prefers deterministic on-meter discounts, but is willing to accept post-hoc credits for a pilot if the math and sampling windows are defined (we'd need the sampling script output two days before invoice close). Can you commit to a daily sampling digest and the exact algorithm (we're fine with a blackbox if the sample output includes input_tokens, cache_hit_tokens, sample_size)?

2) Burst buffer vs pre-paid bucket: we prefer a committed burst pool we can draw down (pre-paid) rather than a per-day overage cap. Can you add a line to the SOW that shows the drawdown order (burst pool first, then committed monthly, then overage)?

3) DocuSign & procurement: please route the final SOW to procurement@ledger.ai and include a DocuSign link. Procurement wants separate billing contact and an invoicing cadence (monthly).

If you can send a one-page term sheet with the sampling output cadence, exact rounding quantum for the pilot (we'll accept 10-token gen quantum), and the drawdown order, procurement will route for signature this week.

Thanks — copying Procurement.

— Aisha
Lead Product Ops, Ledger.ai
